decisions.reason: The caption typography specification does not change the PBU naming prefix, naming language, applicability condition, or covered style categories.
The message separately reports missing theme colors, already represented as a same-message runtime failure; the caption typography change does not alter the theme-color requirement state.
Adding caption typography details does not change the existing requirement to apply the specified style system consistently across all templates.
The green level-four bullet is a separate clause already represented by same-message bullet-specific events; the caption typography modification does not alter bullet formatting state.
The caption typography specification does not change legacy source templates, migration targets, or expected copy-paste stability.
Image and table caption typography has no necessary effect on manual line-break entry after pasted content.
The reference to table text labels concerns typography, not table layout stability, column boundaries, or the existing feasibility conflict.
The caption typography change does not alter Tab-driven level transitions, list hierarchy, alignment, or the unresolved style-ribbon conflict.
Table-label typography does not change the requirement that pasted right-hand columns remain within page margins.
The caption typography specification does not change numbered-list alignment or multi-digit numbering behavior.
The supported Microsoft Word environment and general operational-reliability constraint remain unchanged.
The caption font, size, and italic styling do not change document content language or default language configuration.
